clue.text: Like to strip — backed out

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of in the manner of

indicators.note: backed means the word for strip is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to peel is to strip off a layer

explanation.surface: A would-be stripper loses their nerve and pulls out of the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'backed out' but stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sound asleep is out cold, so out is an informal synonym.

clue.text: Shared philosophy classes, frequently around at the same time

parts.note: school can mean lessons or classes, as in no school today

indicators.note: around means the word for frequently surrounds the word for at the same time

parts.note: oft is an old word for often, frequently
though means however, at the same time

explanation.surface: A philosophy course is often taught in concurrent classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of opinion held in common by a group of thinkers is a shared philosophy.

clue.text: Getting away — fancy day off

indicators.note: off means the day letter is taken away

parts.note: a delusion is a fancy, a false belief

explanation.surface: Escaping work: what an imaginative day off feels like.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the act of evading or escaping, so it is a getting away.

clue.text: Model here — get a paper to begin with

definitions.text: Model here — get a paper to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with means only the first letter of paper is taken
model means to shape, so the letters are reshaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Where to find a glamour model: buy a tabloid and turn to the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a noun but is a verb, the anagram signal. Read again, the whole clue describes the topless pin-up that sat near the front of The Sun, a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun tabloid long ran a topless model on its third sheet, so the phrase names that pin-up slot.

clue.text: Popular dancer having taken to drink makes mistakes — bad ones

indicators.note: having taken means the dancer's name holds the drinking word within it

parts.note: Ed Balls, the former Labour politician, was a crowd favourite on the BBC dance show Strictly Come Dancing
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A well-loved dancer hits the bottle and starts fluffing the steps badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls, once a UK government minister, became a much-loved contestant on Strictly Come Dancing in 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: A balls-up is coarse British slang for a botched job, a serious blunder.

clue.text: Treatment from top Eastern doctor accepted

indicators.note: accepted means the word for top takes the other letters into itself

parts.note: best means top, finest

explanation.surface: Care offered by a leading Eastern physician has been taken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being confined to lie down for recovery is a common medical prescription.

clue.text: Carly's condemned loutish habit on roads (and pavements)?

definitions.note: habit here means clothing, the stretchy kit of aggressive cyclists

indicators.note: condemned suggests something wrecked and ruined, so the letters of the name are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Carly has denounced yobbish behaviour on roads and pavements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like behaviour but means garb: British papers call rude cyclists 'Lycra louts', and the bracket hints they ride on pavements too.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretchy cycling wear is the outfit of so-called louts on bikes, so it is their habit, in the clothing sense.

clue.text: Trump's British counterpart's the woman for you — an old nag!

indicators.note: for means the woman word stands in place of the you letter

parts.note: Alan Sugar hosted the British version of The Apprentice, which Donald Trump fronted in the US
U is text speak for you
her means the woman

explanation.surface: Trump's opposite number in Britain: she's the one for you, the old bag!
explanation.walkthrough: 'The woman' tempts SHE; it is HER that fits. Shergar was a Derby-winning racehorse famously kidnapped in Ireland in 1983.
explanation.definitionFit: Nag is slang for a horse, and this celebrated racehorse vanished decades ago.

clue.text: "Drinking one beer in there won't hurt" — department have a wild night out

indicators.note: drinking means the beer word swallows the one word

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer
a is the indefinite article, meaning one

indicators.note: in means the scrambled letters go inside the word there

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: hurt means the letters of won't are damaged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, letters only

explanation.surface: A colleague reassures: one drink in that place does no harm, before the office goes on a riotous spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hurt' turns WON'T into TOWN, which goes 'in' THERE to give THE TOWN RE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go out and celebrate riotously, a wild night on the town.

clue.text: Shut up, Rocky appeared to be indifferent

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
rocky terrain is rugged

explanation.surface: Told to be quiet, a tough guy just looked as if he didn't care.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the shoulders is the gesture of not caring, so doing it shows indifference.

clue.text: Trust councillor's correct

parts.note: to edit is to correct text

explanation.surface: Trust a local councillor to be right.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone credit means believing them; trust and credit are synonyms here.

clue.text: One wet area turned into somewhere drier

indicators.note: turned means the joined pieces are flipped to read backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
a bog is a marshy, wet area

explanation.surface: A marsh dries out and becomes a more arid place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is the great desert of Mongolia and China, about as dry a spot as exists.

clue.text: Afterwards errancy's corrected with tough punishment … or maybe not

parts.note: then means afterwards

indicators.note: corrected means the letters of errancy and tough are put into a different, proper order

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing is put right afterwards with a stern penalty, or perhaps not so stern.
explanation.walkthrough: The '… or maybe not' hints that this sanction for children is barely a punishment at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sent to sit in a set spot is a mild time-out for misbehaving children, arguably hardly a penalty.

clue.text: See 12
Those people outside bend the rule of God

indicators.note: outside means the word for those people goes round the curve word

parts.note: they means those people
an arch is a bend or curve

explanation.surface: Some people step outside convention and bend the divine law.
explanation.definitionFit: Formed from Greek theos and -archy, the word means government by a deity, a theocracy.

clue.text: Shocking! George is rampaging round university

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go about the university letter
rampaging means running wild, so the letters of George is are thrown about

explanation.surface: Outrage! George is running riot around campus.
explanation.definitionFit: An egregious act is outstandingly bad, which is shocking.

clue.text: Followers, once having changed sides, totally exposed

indicators.note: changing sides swaps left for right; once means only one swap is made, so the existing right letter stays

parts.note: stalkers are people who follow someone

explanation.surface: Former fans who switched allegiance have been laid bare.
explanation.walkthrough: Change L (left) to R (right) in STALKERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Starkers is British slang for stark naked, so it means entirely uncovered.

clue.text: About to pick up Boris's book

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: to pick up means to catch the sound of the name as heard

parts.note: Boris Becker is the German tennis champion, whose surname said with no final r gives these sounds

explanation.surface: About to collect Boris's novel from somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boris' tempts the British politician Boris Johnson, but it is the tennis player Becker.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier's 1938 novel bears this title, so it is a book.

clue.text: Moved paper getting thrown around

indicators.note: around means the throwing word goes about the newspaper letters

parts.note: shied means thrown, as at a coconut shy
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper gets tossed about and ends up somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift something is to move it, so the past tenses are synonyms.

clue.text: Politically correct but pointless, OK?

indicators.note: pointless means the compass point north is dropped

parts.note: right-on is slang for politically correct

explanation.surface: A sneer at political correctness: right-minded, yes, but lacking a point, agreed?
explanation.walkthrough: N is one of the compass points, so 'pointless' takes it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Righto is a chirpy British way of saying all right or agreed.

clue.text: Sparkle in bed at end of evening

indicators.note: at means the bedding word sits right after that final letter
end of means only the final letter of evening is used

parts.note: litter is straw bedding for animals

explanation.surface: A twinkle in bed as the evening draws to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitter is a shimmering brightness, a synonym for sparkle.

clue.text: Lead left separately working out what he expects to get

indicators.note: separately means the left letter goes in at its own place, apart from the metal symbol
out means the working word sits outside the metal symbol, enclosing it

parts.note: toiling means working hard
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

explanation.surface: A leading actor, left on their own, works out what they are due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the star of the show, which 'he' points back to, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A headline star expects their name to appear first and largest on posters and credits.

clue.text: Ladies under pressure at first in plant

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of each of the three words is taken

explanation.surface: Women under strain at the start of their life in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory, but here it is a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden flower with tall spires of blooms.

clue.text: Area of Ohio was home to some Americans

indicators.note: area of means a stretch within the words Ohio was supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A region of Ohio once housed a group of US citizens.
explanation.definitionFit: This midwestern US state is where some Americans live.

clue.text: Goods stored in purple round food container

indicators.note: stored in means the goods letters are put within the colour word
round means the colour word is turned about

parts.note: puce is a purplish-brown colour
G is good, so two of them give goods

explanation.surface: Merchandise is kept inside something purple and round that holds food.
explanation.definitionFit: This small cup holds a boiled egg at the breakfast table.

clue.text: Comedy family (rag-and-bone men) are caught inside

indicators.note: caught inside means the letter is trapped within the collectors' word

parts.note: totter is a dated British word for a rag-and-bone man, a scrap collector
R is the abbreviation for are, as in text speak

explanation.surface: A sitcom household of scrap dealers turns out to be trapped indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag-and-bone men suggests Steptoe and Son, but the family is the Trotters of Only Fools and Horses, a British TV sitcom about market traders.
explanation.definitionFit: Del Boy and Rodney's household in the BBC sitcom Only Fools and Horses bear this surname.

clue.text: Randiest when getting massage — that's awkward

indicators.note: getting massage means the letters of randiest are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: The randiest client getting a rubdown makes for an uncomfortable moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A strained conversation is tense and uncomfortable, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Way to travel — walk

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to ride is to travel

explanation.surface: A list of ways of getting about: travel, or walk.
explanation.definitionFit: To move with long, purposeful steps is to walk in a particular way.
